![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14036389/assets/d43fa0efcfb8788316c86958b1175741c136588e81a8119131d1ca0f8d8ee229.png)

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of four line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,-2),$ the line segment for $x\in [-2,-1),$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,1),$ and the line segments for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-2).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,-1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-1.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =1-1+2-2 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for x∈[−3,−2), the line segment for x∈[−2,−1), the line segment for x∈[−1,1), and the line segments for x∈[1,3]. Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows: ∫−33f(x)dx=∫−3−2f(x)dx⏟A1+∫−2−1f(x)dx⏟−A2+∫−11f(x)dx⏟A3+∫13f(x)dx⏟−A4

  • The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−3,−2). The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula A1=12bh=12⋅1⋅2=1.

  • The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−2,−1). The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula A2=12bh=12⋅1⋅2=1. Since the region lies below the x-axis, we have ∫−2−1f(x)dx=−A2=−1.

  • The 3rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−1,1). The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula A3=12bh=12⋅2⋅2=2.

  • The 4th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[1,3]. The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula A4=12bh=12⋅2⋅2=2. Since the region lies below the x-axis, we have ∫13f(x)dx=−A4=−2.

Finally, we obtain ∫−33f(x)dx=A1−A2+A3−A4=1−1+2−2=0.
